newsitem.title: USA: Globalization poses risk, opportunity US bonds-PSA.
newsitem.headline: Globalization poses risk, opportunity US bonds-PSA.

text.p: Fixed-income markets, particularly U.S. Treasury bonds, face major challenges and opportunities as the global economy expands in the years ahead, a top bond market official said on Saturday.

John Meehan, 1997 chairman of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association and managing director of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, warned that foreign appetite for U.S. government debt could be reduced under three circumstances.

They are if the U.S. budget deficit continues to grow, nationwide savings remain low, and the European Monetary Union's single currency unit gains widespread acceptance as a competing reserve currency, Meehan said in a keynote speech at PSA's annual meeting here this weekend.

But Meehan also said opportunities abound for fixed-income markets as the global economy expands. He said local debt markets could sprout in parts of the globe that desperately need to finance new roads, bridges and other infrastructure.
Examples are Eastern Europe, the former Soviet Union and developing countries of East and Southeast Asia, he said.

Also, nations trying to qualify for entry into the European Monetary Union may experiment with local borrowing as they try to contain their national debt levels, Meehan said. That means U.S. public finance professionals could export their expertise, Medehan said.
"Bottom line is that progress is good and ultimately has improved our quality of life, despite some near-term dislocations," Meehan said.
He cautioned dealers that globalization is not a one-way street with just U.S. firms expanding their reach internationally.
Through three quarters of 1996, foreign direct investment in the U.S. approached a $100 billion annual pace -- nearly 25 percent greater than U.S. direct investment abroad, Meehan said.
